lead: Six unique venues along almost two kilometres of the old Turia riverbed. Valencia’s most recognisable architectural icon and one of the most spectacular cultural complexes in Europe.

The City of Arts and Sciences stretches for almost two kilometres along the old bed of the River Turia, at the southern end of Valencia. The work of two Spanish architects of international standing – Santiago Calatrava and Félix Candela – the complex combines interactive science, Europe’s largest aquarium, opera, IMAX cinema and Mediterranean gardens in an architectural setting without equal.

To get the most out of the complex, we recommend setting aside a full day, although each venue can be visited independently. Buying tickets online in advance is always the best option to avoid queues and get the best prices.

items.title: Oceanogràfic
items.subtitle: Europe’s largest aquarium
items.body: With around 45,000 specimens of more than 500 marine species, the Oceanogràfic is the largest aquarium in Europe and a world reference in marine research and conservation. Its buildings, designed by Félix Candela with roofs shaped like flowers and shells, house ecosystems from the Mediterranean, the Arctic, the Tropics and the Antarctic.
facts: Walk surrounded by sharks and rays in a glass-walled passage
Daily show with bottlenose dolphins in an outdoor space
Polar species in facilities adapted to their natural habitat
From €39.45 adult · From €29.65 reduced · Free for under-3s

items.title: Hemisfèric
items.subtitle: The eye of knowledge: 3D cinema and planetarium
items.body: The most photogenic building in the CAC, designed by Santiago Calatrava as an enormous eye reflected in the lake. It houses three projection systems and a 900 m² concave screen: IMAX Dome cinema, 3D digital cinema and a digital projection system for astronomy shows. The films are educational and last roughly 45 minutes.
facts: The largest in Spain, with IMAX Dome technology
High-definition screenings with an immersive three-dimensional effect
Astronomy shows of the night sky
Several screenings a day on astronomy, nature and exploration
From 6 years old · Adults and families

items.title: Museu de les Ciències
items.subtitle: Interactive science inside a dinosaur skeleton
items.body: With more than 26,000 m² of exhibitions, the Museu de les Ciències is a world leader in interactive science communication. Its building, designed by Calatrava to evoke the skeleton of a living creature, hosts permanent and temporary exhibitions on science, technology, nature and evolution, as well as workshops, science shows and a space simulator.
facts: More than 26,000 m² of science to explore, touch and experiment with
Musical and science shows included in general admission
An extra €3.50 experience to live a space flight
Until April 2026: machines and inventions by the Renaissance genius
All ages · Especially for children and young people

items.title: Palau de les Arts Reina Sofía
items.subtitle: The great temple of opera and the performing arts
items.body: Home to Valencia’s opera, ballet, symphonic concerts and performing arts. With 40,000 m² of floor area and a silhouette that evokes a helmet or an enormous sea creature stranded in the Turia riverbed, the Palau de les Arts is one of the most spectacular auditoriums in the world. The arts season runs from mid-September to early July.
facts: Seats 1,700 for opera, ballet and large-scale shows
Chamber hall seating 400 for recitals and intimate concerts
Guided tours of the building’s interior with a separate ticket
Opera, ballet and concerts of the highest international level
Architectural tour from €14 · Shows as scheduled

items.title: Umbracle
items.subtitle: The Mediterranean garden among sculptures and the lake
items.body: A landscaped garden of more than 17,000 m² raised above the complex’s car park, open and free to enter. Mediterranean and subtropical plants grow among its concrete and metal arches, and large-format marble and granite sculptures are on display. On summer nights it becomes one of the most distinctive nightlife spaces in Valencia.
facts: The only CAC venue with free entry all year round
Eight large-format works in marble and granite on the Paseo del Arte
Orange trees, palm trees, bougainvillea and more than 100 plant species
Terrace and special events under the stars in the warm months
Free · Open access all year round
Open during the complex’s opening hours

items.title: Àgora · CaixaForum València
items.subtitle: Art, culture and exhibitions at the heart of the complex
items.body: The Àgora, designed by Calatrava, houses CaixaForum València, a multipurpose cultural space with an annual programme of international art exhibitions, lecture series, concerts, shows and educational workshops. Located between the Assut de l’Or Bridge and the Oceanogràfic, it also has a bookshop and a restaurant. Access to the building is free; the exhibitions require a ticket.
facts: Contemporary art, science and culture from around the world
A varied cultural programme for all audiences
Educational activities for children and families every weekend
With views of the complex’s lake, open from 8:00 to 00:00

items.title: Bus
items.body: Lines 13, 14, 15, 19, 35, 40, 94 and 95 · Lines 95 and 15 go direct to the Oceanogràfic

items.title: Metro
items.body: Lines 3, 5, 7 and 9 · Alameda stop · 15 min on foot along the Turia Gardens

items.title: Bicycle
items.body: Along the Turia Gardens · Continuous cycle lane from the historic centre

items.title: Car
items.body: Own car park at the Umbracle · €7/day with a ticket to any venue

blocks.title: Tips for visiting the City of Arts and Sciences
items: Buy tickets online in advance to avoid queues and secure a time slot at the Hemisfèric
The 3-venue pass is valid for consecutive days: ideal for spreading out your visit
The Umbracle is free and open to everyone: the best place for photos of the complex
Set aside at least a full day if you want to visit the Oceanogràfic and the Museu de les Ciències
Parking drops to €7/day if you show your ticket for any venue
The València Tourist Card gives 10% off most tickets
